slope_percent.label: Slope
slope_percent.description: Steepness of the ramp. A wheelchair user can manage up to about 10% (a 1 cm rise per 10 cm of length) without exhausting effort.

width_cm.label: Width
width_cm.description: Clear travel width. 100 cm lets a single wheelchair pass; wider lets two people pass each other.

height_cm.label: Height
height_cm.description: Total vertical rise the ramp covers, used to gauge whether the slope is sustainable over its length.

door_width_cm.label: Door Width
door_width_cm.description: Clear opening when the doors are fully open. 90 cm fits a standard wheelchair plus its handgrips.

cabin_width_cm.label: Cabin Width
cabin_width_cm.description: Inside width of the cabin. 120 cm gives a wheelchair user enough room to fit comfortably.

cabin_depth_cm.label: Cabin Depth
cabin_depth_cm.description: Inside depth front-to-back. 140 cm lets a wheelchair turn or fit beside another passenger.

height_cm.label: Curb Height
height_cm.description: Step from sidewalk to road. Above ~15 cm without a curb ramp blocks wheels and walkers.

width_cm.label: Width
width_cm.description: Usable walking width (ignore lamp posts and benches). 150 cm lets two wheelchairs pass each other.

width_cm.label: Width
width_cm.description: Clear opening when the door is fully open. 90 cm fits a standard wheelchair.

threshold_height_cm.label: Threshold Height
threshold_height_cm.description: The lip at the bottom of the doorway. Above ~0.6 cm catches small front wheels on a wheelchair.

riser_cm.label: Riser Height
riser_cm.description: Height of each step. Above 16 cm gets exhausting and risky for people with mobility limits.

tread_cm.label: Tread Depth
tread_cm.description: Front-to-back depth of each step. Below 27 cm is too narrow to land a whole foot safely.

signal_duration_sec.label: Signal Duration
signal_duration_sec.description: How long the walk signal stays on. 15 s is enough for a slow walker to cross a typical street.

crossing_width_cm.label: Crossing Width
crossing_width_cm.description: Width of the marked crossing. 300 cm fits two wheelchairs passing in opposite directions.

dropped_curb_height_cm.label: Dropped Curb Height
dropped_curb_height_cm.description: Step from the crossing onto the sidewalk. Above ~1.3 cm catches wheels and trips canes.

slope_percent.label: Slope
slope_percent.description: Steepness of the curb ramp. 8% is the comfortable maximum for a person pushing themself in a wheelchair.

width_cm.label: Width
width_cm.description: Width of the ramp surface. 120 cm matches the wheelchair-friendly minimum.

lip_height_cm.label: Lip Height
lip_height_cm.description: Bump where the ramp meets the road. Above 1.3 cm jolts wheels and trips canes.

door_width_cm.label: Door Width
door_width_cm.description: Clear opening when the door is fully open. 90 cm fits a standard wheelchair.

turning_space_cm.label: Turning Space
turning_space_cm.description: Open circle of clear floor space. 150 cm lets a wheelchair turn fully around.

sink_height_cm.label: Sink Height
sink_height_cm.description: Top of the sink rim from the floor. Below 85 cm lets a seated user reach the tap.

grab_bar_height_cm.label: Grab Bar Height
grab_bar_height_cm.description: Height of the grab bars from the floor. 70 cm or higher lines up with most transfer holds.

mounting_height_cm.label: Mounting Height
mounting_height_cm.description: Center of the sign from the floor. 120-160 cm aligns with eye level for both standing and seated users.

text_height_mm.label: Text Height
text_height_mm.description: Height of the letterforms. Below 15 mm is hard to read from door distance.

welcome.title: Welcome to Mapcess
welcome.tip: A quick tour of the four most common things people report — ramps, sidewalks, elevators, and doors — and how to file your first report in under a minute.

ramps.title: Ramps
ramps.bullet2: Clear width ≥ 100 cm — room for a walker + helper
ramps.bullet3: Handrails on both sides at 90 cm (extra rail at 70 cm for shorter users)
ramps.bullet4: Tactile warning strip at the top and bottom of the ramp

sidewalks.title: Sidewalks
sidewalks.bullet1: Clear width ≥ 150 cm — wheelchairs need to pass each other
sidewalks.bullet2: Overhead clearance ≥ 220 cm — no low branches or signs
sidewalks.bullet3: Contrasting strip along the curb edge so it's visible against the road

elevators.title: Elevators
elevators.bullet1: Door clear width ≥ 90 cm when fully open
elevators.bullet2: Braille labels on every button and voice announcement
elevators.bullet3: Visual floor display + flashing emergency alarm

doors.title: Doors
doors.bullet1: Clear width ≥ 90 cm when fully open
doors.bullet2: Lever handle (not a knob) — easier with weak grip
doors.bullet3: Glass panels marked with contrasting bands at eye level

howTo.title: How to file a report
howTo.tip: Once five neighbours agree, your report becomes verified and starts shaping accessible routes for everyone.
